title: React Hooks Deep Dive
description: Unlock the full power of React hooks. Master useEffect for side effects, useRef for DOM access, useMemo and useCallback for performance, and build your own custom hooks to extract reusable logic.
learningObjectives: Fetch data and manage side effects with useEffect
Understand the dependency array and avoid stale closures
Access DOM elements directly with useRef
Optimise renders with useMemo and useCallback
Extract and share logic with custom hooks

sections.content: A side effect is any operation that reaches outside a component: API calls, timers, subscriptions, DOM mutations, localStorage reads. useEffect is React's dedicated hook for managing these.

exercises.question: What does an empty dependency array [] in useEffect mean?
options: The effect runs on every render
The effect never runs
The effect runs once after the initial render only
The effect runs only when state changes
exercises.correctAnswer: The effect runs once after the initial render only
hints: No dependencies = nothing can trigger it to re-run
exercises.explanation: useEffect(() => {}, []) runs once after the first render and never again. No deps = no triggers. This is how you implement componentDidMount-equivalent logic (like one-time data fetches).

exercises.question: How does changing ref.current differ from calling a state setter?
options: ref.current changes cause re-renders, state does not
No difference — both cause re-renders
Changing ref.current does NOT cause a re-render
refs can only store DOM elements
exercises.correctAnswer: Changing ref.current does NOT cause a re-render
hints: Refs are a 'box' that holds a value, not reactive state
exercises.explanation: Mutating ref.current doesn't trigger a re-render — that's the key difference from state. Use refs when you need to persist a value across renders without triggering updates (timers, previous values, DOM nodes).

sections.content: ⚠️ Don't over-optimize. useMemo and useCallback add complexity and their own overhead. Only add them after profiling confirms a real performance problem.

exercises.question: useCallback is primarily used to:
options: Cache expensive calculations
Prevent a function from being recreated on every render
Asynchronously fetch data
Replace useEffect for callbacks
exercises.correctAnswer: Prevent a function from being recreated on every render
hints: Memoizes a function, not a value
exercises.explanation: useCallback returns a memoized function reference. Without it, a new function object is created every render — which causes child components wrapped in React.memo to re-render even when nothing changed.

sections.content: A custom hook is any function starting with 'use' that calls other hooks. It's how you share stateful logic between components without HOCs or render props. Each component gets its own isolated state.

exercises.question: What is required for a function to be a valid custom React hook?
options: It must be defined in a separate file
It must accept props as arguments
Its name must start with 'use'
It must call at least 3 built-in hooks
hints: React's linting rules check for this convention
exercises.explanation: Custom hooks must start with 'use' — this lets React's linter enforce the Rules of Hooks (hooks can't be called conditionally). The function just needs to start with 'use'; it doesn't need to return anything specific.

sections.content: 1. Only call hooks at the top level — never inside conditions, loops, or nested functions. 2. Only call hooks from React function components or custom hooks — never from regular functions.

exercises.question: When should you prefer useReducer over multiple useState calls?
options: Always — useReducer is always better
When state is a single value
When state logic is complex, state values depend on each other, or next state depends on previous
When you don't want components to re-render
exercises.correctAnswer: When state logic is complex, state values depend on each other, or next state depends on previous
hints: It follows the Redux pattern for a reason
exercises.explanation: useReducer excels when you have multiple state values that change together, complex update logic, or when testing state transitions in isolation is important. For simple independent values, useState is simpler.

capstoneProject.title: GitHub User Search
capstoneProject.description: Build a GitHub user search app that fetches from the GitHub API and displays profiles — using all hooks from this module.
requirements: useFetch custom hook handles all data fetching with loading/error states
useLocalStorage custom hook persists search history
useDebounce custom hook delays API calls while typing
Search input uses useRef for auto-focus
User profile displays avatar, bio, repos, followers
Repo list is filtered client-side — filter logic memoized with useMemo
useReducer manages the app's complex state (query, results, history, filter)
